binaries.name: zeek
binaries.why: Turn a capture into structured logs per protocol — conn, dns, http, ssl, files — which is the form every later question wants.

install.apt: pinned download 8.0.10 (install.download): the Zeek project's own Debian 12 package, zeek-8.0-core, from https://software.opensuse.org/download.html?project=security%3Azeek&package=zeek (zeek is in neither Debian's nor Ubuntu's archive)

binaries.name: tshark
binaries.why: Dissect a capture with a display filter and export fields. Reads far more protocols than any tool here.

binaries.name: capinfos
binaries.why: Report capture format, packet count, time range, snap length, encapsulation and integrity before analysis.

binaries.name: editcap
binaries.why: Deduplicate, split and convert captures while preserving the original evidence.

binaries.name: mergecap
binaries.why: Merge related capture segments into a time-ordered working copy.

binaries.name: text2pcap
binaries.why: Turn a byte-oriented hex dump into a capture for protocol dissection without altering the source.

binaries.name: tcpdump
binaries.why: Apply BPF filters, inspect capture headers and make lossless filtered working captures with the standard examiner CLI.

binaries.name: tcpflow
binaries.why: Reassemble each TCP session into its own file, which is how a transferred object is recovered from a capture.

binaries.name: tcpick
binaries.why: Reassemble and inspect selected TCP conversations from a capture as a second implementation for overlap and evasion checks.

binaries.name: ngrep
binaries.why: Search packet payloads with a BPF scope and a byte-safe regular expression during rapid triage.

binaries.name: suricata
binaries.why: Run a signature set over a capture. GPL-2.0-only, so it is invoked as an executable and never imported.
